decisions.executionNote: Begin right-hand holder approach with gradual inward yaw and elbow-up continuity; pens are in the left workspace.
Advance right hand toward the holder's outer side while finishing inward-facing orientation; keep left parked.
Replan after rejected suffix: use an oblique holder grasp to stay away from the wrist singularity, with smaller increments.
Close around the holder and make a short test lift. Holder orientation/retention is uncertain after contact, so inspect before transporting.
Test lift showed empty fingers and a displaced holder. Open, clear upward, and reorient for a recovery grasp of the holder on its side.
Align the open right gripper along the fallen holder with a modest downward pitch, moving in small continuous increments.
Use wrist view to bring the holder body toward the open finger center, with a slow descent before closing.
Center on the holder's side, close the right gripper fully, and begin a small retention test lift.
Lift the bracketed holder clear of the table while maintaining a fully closed target; verify retention before upright rotation.
The holder stayed on the table during the lift. Reopen and lower the grasp deeper onto its side, retaining the same continuous arm configuration.
Close at the lower holder-body alignment, pause, then lift briefly to check whether the object follows.
Empty closed fingertips indicate another missed grasp. Reopen and approach farther along the body and lower, so the fingers can straddle rather than touch its upper face.
Relieve the downward contact, correct lateral centering on the holder, then close and test retention with a short lift.
Side approach still appears to skim the holder. Clear upward and change to a more downward grasp across its body, keeping the right elbow up.
Move above the now-visible holder midpoint and finish a downward orientation, leaving clearance for a centered top grasp.
Lower the open overhead grasp toward the holder body, correcting the head/wrist alignment slightly outward and forward.
Descend the centered overhead grasp a little farther, close around the holder body, and lift to check retention.
Holder appears to follow the overhead grasp. Lift it clear and progressively rotate its opening upward while moving toward a central right-side holding position.
The holder is visibly lifted. Bring it inward and turn the grasp toward an upright central presentation, with small continuous wrist increments.
Finish the holder presentation while beginning a gentle left-arm overhead approach to the leftmost cyan pen; keep the holder gripper closed.
Holder is visibly upright; lower it to a convenient held height while aligning the left overhead grasp with the first cyan pen.
Correct the left grasp laterally from the wrist image and lower toward the cyan pen's capped half while keeping the holder steady.
Finish centering over the cyan pen, close near table height, and test the grasp with a short vertical lift.
Lift the visibly bracketed cyan pen and rotate its capped end upward while moving toward the held upright holder.
Transport the retained cyan pen above the holder and progressively orient the left hand inward, keeping both grippers closed.
Finish making the cyan pen vertical and align its lower end over the holder opening without releasing yet.
Correct the cyan pen's visible rightward offset and lower its bottom toward the mouth while holding the holder stationary.
Guide the first pen down through the opening with a small centering correction; retain the grasp until insertion is visible.
The pen's lower end is inside the mouth but has tilted on contact. Release it to settle, then withdraw upward and left to inspect.
First cyan pen remains supported inside the holder. Clear it and begin a downward approach to the black pen lying across the left-center table.
Replan from the unchanged pose after the continuity rejection, using much smaller pitch increments and extra clearance.
Continue toward the black pen's capped half while pitching down in smaller stages, staying above the table.
Complete the downward grasp orientation above the horizontal black pen, leaving clearance for visual centering before the final descent.
Center the black pen between the open fingers using the wrist view, align with its axis, and descend to grasp height.
Make the final wrist-view centering correction, close around the black pen, and lift briefly to test retention.
The black pen is bracketed and follows the fingers. Lift it clear while rotating its long axis toward vertical.
Finish rotating the black pen upright and position it above the free side of the held holder, avoiding the leaning cyan pen.
Lower the black pen's visible lower end into the opening while the cyan pen settles, retaining the grasp for inspection.
Release the black pen with its lower end inside the holder, then withdraw the left hand upward and away to inspect and approach the remaining pens.
Two pens are visibly retained in the holder. Approach the remaining black pen from above and gradually align the left gripper with its length.
Finish the overhead orientation for the remaining black pen and approach its capped half with clearance for wrist-view correction.
Align the open fingers along the remaining black pen and descend toward its capped half using the wrist image.
Close on the centered remaining black pen at table height, then perform a short straight lift to verify retention.
Replan after the lift continuity rejection: retract toward the robot while lifting in smaller increments and gently start tipping the retained black pen upright.
The remaining black pen follows the closed fingers. Lift and carry it inward while rotating toward the upright insertion orientation.
Finish the upright rotation and align the third pen over an unoccupied part of the holder opening, keeping it above the rim.
Lower the third pen toward the open space beside the two inserted pens, making a small fore-aft centering correction.
The third pen is contacting the cyan pen near the mouth. Shift slightly into the adjacent gap, lower, and release to settle inside.
Withdraw from the released third pen so it can settle, then begin orienting for the final cyan pen on the table.
The third pen is resting across the rim rather than upright. Bring the holder slightly inward and approach that pen from above for a corrective grasp.
Center on the pen lying across the rim, close on its body, and lift a small amount to confirm the corrective grasp without disturbing the other two pens.
Lift the corrective grasp clear of the rim and rotate the angled black pen toward tip-up vertical, compensating for its diagonal position in the fingers.
The pen has straightened within the grasp. Remove the extra roll and lower its capped end toward the free side of the opening.
Correct the remaining tilt and guide the capped end into the opening. A previously inserted black pen is now visible on the table and will need recovery.
Move the capped end away from the cyan pen into the left-side gap, lower farther through the rim, and release to settle tip-up.
The pen did not settle upright. Reacquire it near the fingers and lift clear so its lower-end alignment can be checked before another insertion.
The corrective grasp was empty and both black pens are on the table. Clear the holder to the right while beginning an overhead approach to the remaining cyan pen.
Continue the overhead cyan-pen approach with clearance from the held holder, keeping the right grasp fixed.
Finish the downward orientation and lower toward the cyan pen's capped half, maintaining an open grasp for visual alignment.
Separate the holder from the left wrist after visible contact, then resume the cyan-pen approach with a small lateral correction and slow descent.
The holder is clear. Lower the centered left grasp to the cyan pen and close fully, pausing before the retention test.
Lift the bracketed cyan pen and turn it upright while bringing the holder slightly inward, preserving clearance between the hands.
The cyan pen stayed on the table. Reopen and return to a deeper, slightly rearward overhead grasp rather than transporting an empty gripper.
Correct the cyan pen's leftward wrist-image offset and lower the fingers slightly farther before closing; keep the holder still.
Lift the now-centered cyan pen while keeping a closed grasp and rotate it partway upright; verify that it follows before approaching the holder.
The cyan pen is retained but close to the holder. Lift it clear and finish making it vertical before attempting alignment over the opening.
The holder appears to have slipped during contact. Keep the second cyan pen raised while reopening and lowering the right hand to recover the holder body.
The holder is upright again. Move the right fingers farther around its body without pressing downward, close, and test a small lift while keeping the cyan pen aloft.
The right fingers closed above the holder body. Reopen and approach lower around the body while keeping the retained cyan pen safely raised.
Close around the lower holder body and lift gently to verify that it follows, keeping the second cyan pen stationary overhead.
The holder follows the right hand. Correct the second cyan pen's visible tilt while keeping it clear above the rim; its orientation within the grasp is uncertain.
Replan after the continuity rejection with smaller pitch steps and a slight retreat to preserve elbow-up reach margin while straightening the pen.
Continue straightening the retained cyan pen in small increments and move its lower end toward the opening without descending yet.
Guide the nearly vertical cyan pen toward the clear right side of the opening and lower its end inside, keeping both grasps closed.
The new pen is resting on the first pen's cap, not entering the free opening. Lift off, correct its contact-induced tilt, and shift toward the unoccupied back side.
Align the now-upright pen's lower end over the free portion of the mouth and lower cautiously, maintaining clearance from the first pen.
